html:
Tvrtko I was the first king of Bosnia, ruling from 1353 and crowned king in 1377, who made Bosnia for a time the strongest state in the western Balkans.

He came to power as a boy ban under the overlordship of Hungary, then broke free of it. After the Serbian Nemanjić line died out he claimed descent from it and was crowned King of the Serbs and Bosnia, probably at Mile near Visoko. He took part of the Adriatic coast and Dalmatian towns, and sent troops to the Battle of Kosovo in 1389. His kingdom grew rich on silver mines and trade with Ragusa. After his death in 1391 the nobles weakened the crown, and the kingdom fell to the Ottomans in 1463.
sum: Tvrtko I was the first king of Bosnia, ruling from 1353 and crowned king in 1377, who made Bosnia for a time the strongest state in the western Balkans.
